---
title: "Extension or polyfill"
---

phit has two implementations of the same `Phit\` functions:

- **The extension**, `phpstats/phit`, is compiled Rust installed into PHP with
  PIE or a prebuilt binary. See [Installation](installation.qmd).
- **The polyfill**, `phpstats/phit-polyfill`, is plain PHP installed with
  Composer. It needs no PHP extension.

```sh
composer require phpstats/phit-polyfill
```

Code written against one runs unchanged on the other. Each polyfill release
reproduces one phit release. Polyfill 0.3.0 reproduces phit v0.3.0, 0.2.0
reproduces v0.2.0, and 0.1.0 reproduces v0.1.1.

## How they coexist

Composer loads the polyfill's `bootstrap.php` through its `files` autoload. If
`extension_loaded('phit')` is true, the bootstrap returns before defining
anything, so every `Phit\` function is the extension's. Installing both is
therefore safe: the extension is used where it is loaded, and the polyfill
everywhere else, such as a CI runner or a host where extensions cannot be
installed.

The polyfill does not fill gaps in an older extension. If the loaded extension
is older than the polyfill's phit release, the functions added since then stay
undefined.

The polyfill's composer.json declares `"provide": {"ext-phit": "*"}`. A package
that requires `ext-phit` is therefore satisfied by the polyfill, including one
that uses the functions the polyfill lacks.

## What the polyfill covers

The polyfill provides 232 of phit 0.3.0's 233 functions. It does not provide
`Phit\read_csv()` or the `Phit\CsvReader` class. Without the extension,
`function_exists('Phit\read_csv')` and `class_exists('Phit\CsvReader')` return
false, and `Phit\Polyfill::supports('Phit\read_csv')` returns false.

| Area | Polyfill |
| --- | --- |
| Formula models and prediction | `model_matrix`, `fit_lm`, `fit_glm`, `fit_lmer`, `fit_glmer` and `predict`, with a port of the extension's formula parser |
| Matrix models | All seven `fit_*` matrix functions |
| Mixed models | The same structures as the extension: `fit_lmer` with random intercepts and slopes, `(x || g)`, several terms and nesting, by REML or ML with BOBYQA or Nelder–Mead; `fit_glmer` with one binomial logit `(1 | g)`, by Laplace or adaptive quadrature with up to 61 points |
| Distributions, descriptive statistics, seeded sampling | All functions |
| Posterior-draw kernels | `draws_moments`, `draws_covariance_map` and `draws_affine` |
| CSV input | Not provided; phibble's `DataFrame::fromCsv()` falls back to its own PHP reader |

The polyfill's test suite runs the extension's reference fixtures, including
the lme4 and seeded-sampling references, at the extension's tolerances.
Randomized parity tests compare its results with the extension's. In those
tests the posterior-draw kernels and the random-intercept and random-slope
fits are bit-identical.

## Differences

- The listwise-deletion warning is `E_USER_WARNING` in the polyfill and
  `E_WARNING` in the extension. The text is the same.
- Arguments of the wrong scalar type follow PHP's userland rules in the
  polyfill: coercion, or a `TypeError` under `strict_types`.
- Every polyfill function throws an exception with code 1007 while OPcache's
  JIT is compiling the process. The JIT has produced wrong numerical results
  in the polyfill, so the polyfill refuses to run under it. PHP 8.4 and 8.5
  disable the JIT by default. PHP 8.3's default settings (`opcache.jit=tracing`
  with `opcache.jit_buffer_size=0`) also leave it off. The extension runs under
  any JIT setting.
- On an x86-64 CPU without fused multiply-add, the extension's products of
  matrices larger than 5×5 can differ from the polyfill's in the last bit.

## Speed

The polyfill is slower, and the gap grows with model size. These timings were
recorded on an Apple M5 Ultra with PHP 8.5.10, OPcache on and the JIT off.

| Fit | Recorded | Polyfill | Extension | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fit_ols`, n = 100,000, 10 predictors | 2026-10-28, polyfill ab803fd, phit 3861d77 | 262 ms | 29 ms | 9.1× |
| `fit_logistic`, same design | 2026-10-28, polyfill ab803fd, phit 3861d77 | 1.60 s | 72 ms | 22× |
| Mixed model with 120 random coefficients | 2026-10-16 | 8.0 s | 103 ms | 78× |

Mixed models ran 13 to 78 times slower in that comparison. The polyfill's cost
grows with roughly the cube of the number of random coefficients.

## Versions and platforms

The polyfill's composer.json requires PHP `^8.3`. Its CI tests PHP 8.3, 8.4
and 8.5 on Linux, in five OPcache and JIT modes, and on macOS in two. Windows
is untested. The extension supports PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 on Linux and macOS.

The polyfill's own documentation is in the
[phit-polyfill repository](https://github.com/phpstats/phit-polyfill).
